name: weekly across spring-forward preserves wall-clock time
why: The canonical case Date-based recurrence libraries get wrong. A 09:00 meeting must stay at 09:00 local while the UTC offset moves -05:00 to -04:00.

name: occurrence inside the spring-forward gap shifts for that day only
why: 02:30 does not exist on 2026-03-08 in New York, so that day moves to 03:30. Every later day must return to 02:30. rrule-temporal carries the shift forward permanently; reanchorWallClock corrects it.

name: ambiguous local time on fall-back resolves to the earlier instant
why: 01:30 happens twice on 2026-11-01 in New York. Temporal's 'compatible' disambiguation picks the first, which is the ICS convention. The wall-clock time is unchanged on every day.
decision: earlier instant (EDT, -04:00) when a local time is ambiguous

name: BYDAY with a negative ordinal selects the last weekday of the month
why: Ordinal BYDAY is where month-length edge cases surface. February 2026 has exactly four Sundays.

name: BYSETPOS selects the last weekday of each month
why: BYSETPOS is frequently unimplemented or wrong. January and February 2026 both end on a weekend, so the answer is not simply the last day.

name: UNTIL is inclusive when it equals an occurrence instant
why: RFC 5545 3.3.10: UNTIL is inclusive. It is UTC-valued even for a zoned DTSTART, which is where off-by-one errors come from. 09:00 EDT is 13:00Z, so the third occurrence lands exactly on UNTIL.

name: monthly on the 31st skips short months rather than clamping
why: RFC 5545: a BYMONTHDAY that does not exist in a month yields no occurrence for that month. Clamping to the 28th would be wrong, and clamping the cursor would corrupt every later month too.

name: monthly with the day implied by DTSTART behaves as if BYMONTHDAY were explicit
why: RFC 5545: absent BYMONTHDAY defaults to DTSTART's day of month, so this must match the explicit case exactly. rrule-temporal instead clamps to Feb 28 AND moves its cursor there, returning Mar 28 and Apr 28 -- wrong even for months that have a 31st. normalizeRule makes the default explicit.

name: yearly on 29 February does not occur in a non-leap year
why: 29 February does not exist in 2025, so the rule yields nothing that year. Falling back to 28 February invents an occurrence the rule never specified.

name: yearly on 29 February lands on the next leap year
why: The other half of the leap-year case: skipping 2025 and 2026 must not consume the COUNT, and 2028 must still be produced.

name: EXDATE removes a matching occurrence
why: Baseline exclusion.

name: EXDATE matches by instant, not by string form
why: The same moment written as a UTC instant must exclude the same occurrence as the local form. 2026-06-02T13:00Z is 09:00 in New York.

name: an occurrence straddling the window start is included
why: The event begins before `from` and is still running at `from`. Filtering on start alone would drop it, and an overnight event would vanish from the morning's view.

name: a zero-duration occurrence exactly at the window start is included
why: Under a plain half-open overlap test, end > from is false when start == end == from, so the event would silently disappear.

name: a zero-duration occurrence exactly at the window end is excluded
why: The window is half-open. The instant `to` belongs to the next window, or it would be returned twice when a client pages through consecutive ranges.

name: an all-day event is visible from a zone where its date has begun
why: ADR-0005: all-day events are floating dates resolved against the caller's rendering zone. In Auckland, 3 October has already started when the window opens.

name: the same all-day event is not yet visible from a zone where its date has not begun
why: The mirror of the previous case, and the reason all-day events cannot carry a stored anchor. In Honolulu, 3 October begins at 10:00Z -- after this window closes. Different answers for different viewers is correct, not a rounding error.

name: a weekly all-day series crosses a DST boundary without artefacts
why: Floating dates have no offset to shift. A weekly all-day event spanning the US spring-forward must land on the same weekday every week, which is the payoff of ADR-0005.

name: a multi-day all-day event straddling the window start is included
why: Exclusive end date, and the sweep must reach back far enough to find a span that began before the window.

name: an all-day event ending exactly at the window start is excluded
why: endDate is EXCLUSIVE (RFC 5545 DTEND for DATE values). A single-day event on 2 June ends at 3 June, which is the instant the window opens, so it does not overlap.

name: a DTSTART not synchronised with the rule is not itself an occurrence
why: RFC 5545 3.3.10 declares this case undefined, so there is no correct answer to inherit. DTSTART is a Sunday; the rule asks for Mondays. We follow the dominant convention and exclude it.
decision: exclude a non-matching DTSTART, matching python-dateutil and rrule.js

name: nominal duration keeps the end wall-clock stable across spring-forward
why: A 09:00-17:00 shift stays 09:00-17:00 on a 23-hour day. Preserving elapsed time instead would show 18:00 twice a year, which reads as a bug to anyone looking at it.
decision: nominal wall-clock duration, not exact elapsed duration
